# Appendix D Experimental Data, Parameter Provenance, and Warehouse-Population Reproducibility

## Sources and verified availability

The scientific input chain begins with the canonical reference workbook and
the full existing/candidate warehouse registry. It does not begin with a map,
a solver output or an unversioned cache. The exact files inspected here are
preserved in the version 0.2.0 input archive identified by the published dataset
receipt. The archive MD5 is `79f85dfe638df1c2dfa5cca9cf343d88`.
Individual workbook SHA256 values, worksheet names, dimensions, original cells
and input/output membership checks are distributed in
`appendix_d_inventory.json`. This is a compact derived metadata record, not
permission to republish every external source or new raw experiment archive.

| Source | Scientific role | Verified location and status | Identity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Canonical reference workbook | Model data, original scenarios, investment/tariff tables and 215-site anchor | Git-tracked `data/templates/`; same bytes in historical input archive | SHA256 prefix de3bdc51… |
| Full warehouse registry | 18,086-record population-selection source | `external-inputs/` member of preserved input archive; not Git-tracked as this workbook | SHA256 prefix 0d19865a… |
| Original population manifest/order | Deterministic ranking, strata, source/anchor identities and seed | Archived processed population records; hash-bound by execution receipts | Manifest 4134147f…; order 7a524b2e… |
| Materialized case workbooks | Effective warehouse population plus approved OSRM distance rows | External processed snapshot, not assumed present in Git from a filename mention | Full hashes in the population table below |
| Scalar evidence archives | Original input, validation, result and resource receipts | External archives, referenced by public review metadata | h215: 81890b54…; h300: dc5969fa…; h400: e0b58bb7… |

The canonical workbook has 14 sheets, including explanatory and control sheets.
The registry's `Sheet1` has 18,087 rows including its header and 13 columns;
`Metodologia` retains its separate descriptive sheet. The template's `Warehouses`
sheet has 216 rows including its header and 25 columns. `Oferta` has 6,301 rows/
6 columns; `Demanda` 4,441/11; `Frete` 28/4; `Tarifa_Armz` 4/5;
`Custo_Invest` 5/6; `Parametros_Modelo` 13/5; `Cenarios` 4/8.
The metadata inventory enumerates the remaining sheets and actual headers.
Dimensions include template/control rows and must not be called model entity
counts. The effective cases have 37 origin identifiers, 27 domestic roles and 10
export roles; geographic coincidences do not merge these identities. The
conceptual reference to eight ports does not replace ten actual export-role
records or assert that each record is a distinct physical port.

## Data dictionary and interpretation

| Effective object | Original source / keys | Meaning and unit | Loader treatment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Supply | `Oferta`: Cidade, Produto, Data, Peso (ton) | Exogenous grain t per origin/product/period | Normalized keys and periods; additive records aggregated, not arbitrarily first-selected |
| Demand | `Demanda`: role, city/ID, product, period, limit rule | Domestic requirement or optional export upper limit, t/period | Separate domestic/export identifiers; fixed versus supply-derived limit retained |
| Facility | `Warehouses`: CDA, Status, coordinates, Tipo, holder | Stable site identity, existing/candidate role, geographic record | CDA preserved; coincident coordinates retain separate facilities |
| Static capacity | Cap. Estática and maximum-capacity columns | t of stock; candidate investment maximum t | Candidate base capacities zero, maximum available investment distinct |
| Handling | Cap. Recepção / Cap. Expedição legacy tonne-labelled columns | Effective daily t/day rates | Multiplied by declared operating days; investment daily gains added consistently |
| Freight | `Frete`: Estado / Frete Tonelada Km | BRL/(t km) | State-derived origin and dispatching-warehouse coefficients |
| Storage | `Tarifa_Armz`: product and public/private tariff | BRL/(t period) | Product/holder mapping, not a one-time capital cost |
| Investment | `Custo_Invest`, explicit or formula-derived warehouse columns | Fixed BRL and variable BRL/investment-t | Explicit values preferred; documented capacity/cost fallback if absent |
| Distance | Approved OSRM `Distancias` and materialization audit | Directed road km | Source/dataset/profile validated; retained graph selected afterward |
| Scenarios | `Cenarios` and optional specific arrays | Dimensionless multipliers and probabilities | Original DET arrays or explicit nine Cartesian STO combinations |
| Initial inventory | Optional original stock records | t by warehouse/product | Missing entries use the established zero convention |

`excel_loader._clean_dataframe`, normalization helpers and `_add_to_mapping`
implement cleaning, stable identifiers and additive record handling. Normalized
duplicates are not universally harmless; aggregation is appropriate only for
the additive source fields. Blank optional attributes and missing mandatory
identities are different conditions. Model validation checks domains, capacities,
route distances and required data. The pipeline is not described as globally
lossless: role splitting, candidate translation, sparse arc selection and
scenario generation change representation or intentionally select a subset.

## Original versus effective parameter values

Four layers must be distinguished: original cell content; its scientific
interpretation and validation; the numerical array supplied to the model; and
the approved rule explaining a difference. The parameter sheet in the following
table is `Parametros_Modelo` in the exact canonical workbook. A blank formula cache is not evidence
of a zero cost. A deliberate approved transformation is not automatically a
spreadsheet error.

| Parameter | Original source fact | Effective rule/value | Unit and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unmet demand penalty | Parameter sheet, B4 = 1000000; A4 identifies the parameter | Dynamic preparation and exact experiment guard; accepted 90000 for every domestic/product entry | BRL/t shortage; original receipts and frozen vector |
| Static exceedance penalty | Parameter sheet, B5 = 1000000 | `50 × reference`; accepted 45000 at every site | BRL per stock-slack t at a period; time sum has t·period |
| Reception overflow penalty | Parameter sheet, B6 = 1000000 | Same reference rule; accepted 45000 at every site | BRL/t reception overflow within period; no extra days factor |
| Candidate investment cost | Registry candidate maximum/opening columns contain placeholders; canonical enhanced cost cells can contain formulas without cached values | `variable_from_total`: total estimate divided by positive maximum capacity, fixed cost zero; documented canonical cost-table fallback when formula caches are absent | BRL/investment-t and BRL fixed; `_load_warehouses` |
| Expansion unit cost | Custo_Invest low/high 600/1200 | Average 900 when the explicit effective value is absent | BRL/expansion-t; loader cost-table average |
| Inventory tariff | `Tarifa_Armz`, Soja 45 and Milho 48 | Effective product/warehouse tariff mapping | BRL/(t period), not USD/t |
| Capacity coupling | Original candidate/handling attributes and model settings | Daily factors: candidate/expansion 0.20 per invested t; conversion 1.0; default 30 days/period | t/day before conversion; conversion does not add static capacity |
| STO probabilities | Template base probability 1, Ativo SIM; low/high probability 0.25, Ativo NAO | Approved supply × demand low/base/high Cartesian design; nine weights of 1/9 | Distinct from reading only the template's active rows |

The original sheet cell values above are exact, not approximate million-real
substitutes. `excel_loader._build_parameter_table` reads explanatory/configuration
parameters, but `_build_penalty_rates` constructs the actual arrays using the
explicit loader policy. The accepted cases select `thesis_dynamic`, not an
automatic pass-through of `Parametros_Modelo!B4:B6`. Initial loader defaults
of 1,000,000 likewise are not the effective executed vector.

`mathematical_contract.prepare_model_data` recomputes and freezes the vector
after route selection. Its reference is the maximum of 100, effective expansion
unit costs and storage tariffs; it is 900 in the accepted cohort. Storage and
reception weights are 50 times that reference. Domestic weights are 100 times
the larger of the reference and the maximum selected final-leg DC/OC freight
cost for each domestic destination, replicated by product. Thus the general
policy can be indexed and topology-dependent. Original accepted receipts show
every effective entry at 90000/45000/45000; operational gates explicitly reject
drift. This appendix does not restore the original cell values, calibrate the
policy, or relabel earlier results under new coefficients.

Monetary labels `$` in the original columns are interpreted as Brazilian reais
under the researcher's clarification. The contextual BRL 5 per USD 1 reference is not
an exchange-rate conversion of results. No new discounting, annualization or
cost-base correction is made. Penalties are artificial feasibility-relaxation
weights, not observed financial expenditures. They relax their specific physical
constraints, not shipping, graph eligibility or every possible infeasibility.
A penalized-objective gap at or below 1% is not a comparable relative guarantee for the
economic subtotal, exact optimality or zero shortage. Search time need not
change monotonically with the weight magnitudes.

## Population selection and nesting

The preserved selection method is nested deterministic proportional strata over
state, warehouse type and static-capacity quartile. Its seed is
`model-agrologistic-v020-warehouse-population-v1`. All 146 existing sites remain;
the 69 canonical candidate anchors begin the ranked candidate sequence. Of 18,086
registry entries, 17,940 are candidates and one nonpositive-static-capacity
candidate is excluded. Original checkpoint levels include 215 and 500, but not 300
or 400. The historical intermediate materialization preserves the candidate
ranking; it is not a resampling or a rewrite of that original manifest.

| Case | Existing / candidates | OSRM workbook SHA256 prefix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| h215 |146 /69|40edb665… (full value in metadata)|
| h300 |146 /154|7761cce7… (full value in metadata)|
| h400 |146 /254|c3085456… (full value in metadata)|
| h500 |146 /354|888fbff4… (full value in metadata)|

Membership was checked by actual CDA identifiers, not counts or coordinate
equality: $W_{215}\subseteq W_{300}\subseteq W_{400}\subseteq W_{500}$.
All eight accepted original `warehouses_used.csv` files match the corresponding
frozen workbook's ordered CDA list exactly. The compact inventory records the
comparison and ordered-ID hashes. Each original attempt retains the complete
ID/role/model-order/stratum/rank list and selection rule; optimized activation,
positive capacity and positive utilization are separate output observations.
The h500 membership check is an input finding only, not an accepted h500 solve.

## Transformation chain and road/scenario inputs

The auditable chain is original workbooks → normalized source records → frozen
population ranking and candidate-cost translation → materialized OSRM distances
→ role/product-specific arcs and sparse selection → original DET or explicit STO
arrays → frozen effective penalties/network → native scalar MILP. The loader
(`load_model_data_from_excel`, `_load_warehouses`, `_load_supply`, `_load_demand`,
`_load_scenarios`) and preparation (`select_routes`, `apply_connectivity_repair`,
`prepare_model_data`) provide the function-level path. Appendix C maps the final
arrays to every equation and solver construction.

Raw OSRM family pairs are not retained product/scenario/period flow variables.
The frozen audits contain 63,289/113,269/190,569/287,869 raw directed pairs for
h215/h300/h400/h500, including optional direct distances. Those distances do
not prove OC was enabled in an optimization. Accepted receipts use W and retain
zero OC; warehouse transshipment remains enabled. The common sparse policy is
20% `connectivity_preserving_pareto`, export coverage `one_sink_per_product`.
Direct-enabled selection can affect repairs or dynamic weights, so its actual
common arc sets and indexed coefficients must be checked before a causal
topology interpretation.

OSRM uses the preserved Brazil dataset, driving profile and MLD fastest-route
configuration. Its audits identify the PBF, OSRM version, container/profile
hashes, cache counts and distance normalization. All four case audits report no
Haversine fallback. The source contains directed distances, not necessarily
route polylines; maps must not fabricate straight road geometry or silently
query live OSRM. The nine controlled STO combinations use supply multipliers
0.85/1/1.15 and domestic-demand multipliers 0.95/1/1.05, each probability 1/9.
They are controlled experiments, not calibrated probabilities or forecasts.

## Evidence snapshots SQLite and access limitations

Accepted original archives retain job 2217990/source 5f73871b… (h215 DET/STO),
2218193/source 04ba9edc… (five h300 STO thread observations), and
2219884/source d9ca710d… (h400 STO). Their input receipts bind workbook and
effective model/network/penalty identities, membership, scenario probabilities
and solver options; completion and independent-validation receipts retain
output/source identities. The editorial `scalar_evidence.json` is a derivative
summary, not a replacement certificate. h500 job 2220382/source fce341df… has no
supplied terminal result at this evidence cutoff.

The separate geographic SQLite stores normalized identities, population
membership, accepted positive flows and available geometry/metadata. It is
reused through source/content keys and opened read-only by Dash/headless
rendering. It is not the authoritative Excel input or a replacement for the
historical OSRM distance cache. Rebuilding a derived visualization database does
not authorize route acquisition, source rewriting or a new optimization.

Researchers can inspect the public canonical workbook, source and published
dataset inventory, and request original restricted material under its applicable
terms. The registry and exact processed inputs were inspected from the preserved
archive; the fact that a file is available locally or in a historical deposit
does not grant blanket new redistribution rights. No private workbook, raw HPC
archive, license or credential is added to this supplementary package. Replaying
an original residual certificate is distinguished from reloading private input
and performing a fresh residual reconstruction or a new mathematical solve.
